title: Enterprise SDK intake: multi-language + streaming auth pattern proposal
creator: Priya Ramanathan
description: Background: Multiple enterprise customers and Solutions Engineering requests in Q4–Q1 asked for a consistent SDK onboarding pattern that supports (1) SSO-first auth (OIDC/SAML) for enterprise orgs, (2) token-based service accounts for CI and server-side use, and (3) lightweight resumable streaming for mobile/edge clients. Problem: existing SDKs are inconsistent across languages (JS/Python strong, Go/C#/Rust fragmented), auth UX differs (manual token minting vs. integrated SSO flows), and streaming ergonomics lack built-in reconnection/backpressure helpers for unstable networks. Goal: define a triage outcome and a recommended implementation plan that balances customer impact, engineering effort, and security review scope. Deliver a prioritized list of language targets, an auth pattern reference (SSO + service-account token exchange + refresh semantics), and a minimal streaming ergonomics spec (resume tokens, reconnect backoff, single-stream multiplexing) for inclusion in SDK design docs and eng tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Product decision documented: recommended auth pattern (SSO-first + short-lived service tokens + refresh flow) and security implications
Language prioritization list agreed with ENG and Solutions (minimum: Go, C#, Rust added to roadmap)
Streaming ergonomics spec approved: resume tokens, idempotent chunking, client-side backpressure API surface
Triage outcome mapped to engineering tickets with estimates and owners
Executive one-pager for enterprise GTM and onboarding created and reviewed by Sales/Success
